about.title: Who I am, what drives me
about.pullquote: I help mid-sized and large organisations bring AI initiatives from idea to production — strategically clarified, technically evidenced, cleanly regulated.
paragraphs: For more than 25 years I was on the market side — at digital agencies and SaaS companies: as key account manager, selling an AI-driven personalisation platform, most recently managing an international portfolio for compliance software across EMEA. Along the way, I also saw implementations fail — almost never on technology, almost always on unclear requirements and absent accountability.

In 2020 I deliberately trained in project management, business analysis, agile methods and IT strategy — not as a collection, but because I no longer wanted to just explain what a system could do. I wanted to understand the system and be accountable for it actually working for the client. Immediately afterwards, as IT project manager, I supported the introduction of a laboratory information system.

Since 2020 I have systematically built five qualification areas, the newest of them AI — each one externally examined and certified. For me that is not a reorientation, but the completion of 25 years at the intersection of leadership, the business and technology. That translation work is what I do best — combined with the technical delivery capability I have been deliberately building since 2025, including with the possibilities of AI.

What drives me is rarely the technology itself. It is the moment a strategic idea becomes a visible result that genuinely moves an organisation forward. I dislike managing a status quo — what interests me is questioning existing processes and making them noticeably better.

Turning complex problems into simple, intuitive solutions that genuinely make people's everyday work easier — that is the challenge that draws me to every new project. Alongside that is a curiosity that never quite settles: every project is also a chance to really understand a new technology, not just know it superficially.

Part of that is being honest about my own limits. Where a project needs a specialist — for training custom learning models, for instance — I say so openly and bring in the right people rather than claim the capability myself. People come before tools, care before speed.

projects.title: Selected projects
projects.lead: Evidence rather than assertion — situation, approach, result.

items.title: Automated Intake and Governance Workflow for First-Contact Inquiries
items.client: Confidential — real estate and financial advisory firm (name withheld at client's request)
items.challenge: A real estate and financial advisory firm was drowning in first-contact inquiries that had to be manually classified, checked for missing information and prioritised — time that was missing from actual advisory work. The intake process needed to move from concept to an actually working, automated system — including error handling, monitoring and a solid economic case.
items.approach: Analysed the process with SIPOC and 5-Whys, then implemented a 21-node workflow in n8n: an AI agent with structured output classifies processing risk and missing information, a switch automatically routes to review, follow-up or governance review, with dedicated error paths for every critical component.
items.result: Delivered and put into production as a client engagement in 2025, with a calculated ROI in the range of roughly 131% over six months.

items.title: My Own Portfolio Website: an AI-Directed Build, from Content System to Deployment
items.role: Client, direction & quality control (built with Claude)
items.challenge: A professional, privacy-first portfolio site needed to exist without tying up weeks of development time better spent on actual consulting work — and without falling back on generic, tracking-heavy website builders.
items.approach: Directed an AI-assisted website build across multiple sessions: clarified requirements and positioning, designed a JSON-driven content system with no framework dependency, iteratively refined design and structure (including a CV design deliberately kept separate from the website design), pushed for SEO and GEO optimisation (llms.txt, JSON-LD, AI-crawler allowlisting) and accessibility, and set up deployment via GitHub and Vercel. Personally diagnosed issues along the way, including a cache-control bug that delayed how updates reached visitors.
items.result: Live and in production since 2025: zero cookies, no tracking, no external fonts — fully static HTML, fully bilingual (DE/EN), with the CV generated from the very same data. Verifiable first-hand at marco-strote.vercel.app.

items.title: Hybrid AI Architecture for a Hardware Advisory Tool
items.client: Training project · WBS module EIOPAN (fictional case company)
items.challenge: Standard product filters do not reliably translate model size, quantisation, context length and use case into a sound hardware recommendation for locally run AI models — risking advice that is either wrong or altogether absent.
items.approach: Hybrid architecture combining a rule-based compatibility engine, versioned fact/benchmark data (RAG) and a language model used strictly for explanation — never for the technical judgement itself. An output validator blocks invented specifications, a reproducible decision record documents every recommendation, backed by four approval gates.
items.result: Rated “absolute professional quality” by the examiner. Hard quality gates fully met: zero invented specifications, 100% source coverage, at least 98% of must-have requirements satisfied. Training project from the WBS AI Consultant program, not a real client engagement.

items.title: AI Roadmap for a First-Contact and Qualification Assistant
items.client: Training project · WBS module KIUSCA (fictional case company)
items.challenge: An owner-run real estate and financial advisory firm was drowning in first-contact inquiries that had to be manually classified, checked for missing information and prioritised — time that was missing from actual advisory work.
items.approach: Built a complete AI roadmap rather than a point solution: use-case assessment with a consultant scorecard and impact-effort matrix, an MS365-adjacent target architecture with human-in-the-loop, a four-week MVPoc with clear target metrics, and a red/amber/green governance gate that keeps decision authority firmly with people.
items.result: The examiner specifically praised the clean separation of “evidenced”, “hypothesis” and “open”, and the traffic-light governance system. Training project from the WBS AI Consultant program, not a real client engagement — shows the methodology is directly transferable to real mandates.

items.q: What role is Marco Strote looking for?
items.a: Both are open: consulting engagements as an independent adviser and a permanent position. Suitable roles include AI consultant, AI governance manager, AI compliance manager, transformation consultant, digitalisation manager, and project or programme lead in a digitalisation context. Interim project leadership mandates are also of interest.

items.q: How does working together on a consulting engagement work?
items.a: That depends heavily on the individual project — complexity, the client's available resources and the timeframe all vary. So I clarify it concretely in the first conversation rather than answering with a standard model.
Immediately. As an independent consultant I am not bound by a notice period and can start at short notice, whether on a project or in a permanent role.
All three work. My base is Wentorf bei Hamburg, and I reach the Hamburg metropolitan region daily without difficulty. For projects further afield I am willing to travel and work remotely in between.

items.q: Why the move from sales to consulting?
items.a: It is less a move than a completion. Selling digital and regulatory solutions, I saw over years where implementations actually fail — almost never on technology, almost always on unclear requirements and absent accountability. In 2020 I acquired the methodological side systematically, then immediately led a system introduction as IT project manager. Today I can serve both sides: explain the value and own the delivery.

items.q: How deep does the governance and EU AI Act experience go?
items.a: The EU AI Act affects not only organisations that build AI, but everyone deploying third-party AI — they count as deployers and have had obligations since February 2025. Full enforcement begins on 2 August 2026, with fines of up to 35 million euros for high-risk systems. I engage intensively with exactly that intersection and document it in my own articles: AI inventory, risk classification under Annex III, governance structures, and the still unsettled question of how agentic AI can be reconciled with the human oversight required by Article 14.

items.q: Don't I also need a data scientist or ML engineer for an AI project?
items.a: Depends on the project. If a custom model needs to be trained or statistically validated, I bring in specialised experts. The role before that — clarifying needs, sharpening goals, translating between leadership, the business and technology — I have covered for 25+ years. I am actively building out the technical integration side: in my AI Consultant certification program I have already delivered several self-built AI applications with top scores. For most organisations, that means an experienced point of contact for strategy and steering, with evidenced technical delivery capability.

items.q: Which industries has Marco Strote worked in?
items.a: Across sectors, I now advise mid-sized and large organisations on AI and digital transformation. At 3E (today owned by New Mountain Capital, formerly Verisk) three years selling EHS and compliance solutions to customers in chemicals, retail and pharma; at 1WorldSync (today part of Syndigo) two years of HazMat compliance solutions with an offering focus on DIY and retail. In between, laboratory and environmental analysis, plus several years of e-commerce for retail companies — at hmmh AG (today part of the Plan.Net Group/Serviceplan, clients including Otto and Tchibo), For Sale Digital (still an independent agency in Hamburg) and Akanoo, an AI start-up with its own prediction algorithms for purchase intent — my earliest AI product experience, back in 2016. Plus sales at Egencia (today part of American Express Global Business Travel). Earlier in my career, controlling roles at SinnerSchrader (today Accenture Song), Kabel New Media and TBG Nord-Beton (then part of the Holcim group).

Fourteen certifications: thirteen from AXELOS and EXIN — ITIL 4 Strategic Leader covering Digital & IT Strategy and Direct, Plan and Improve, plus ITIL 4 Foundation; PRINCE2 Foundation, PRINCE2 Practitioner and PRINCE2 Agile Practitioner; Agile Scrum Foundation, Scrum Master and Scrum Product Owner; EXIN BCS Foundation in Business Analysis together with Practitioner certificates in Business Analysis Practice, Requirements Engineering and Modelling Business Processes — plus the WBS AI Consultant Certificate (expected completion: August 2026).
